raw_case_text: A 28-year-old male from Santarem, Para, Brazil, with a history of leisure activities in a rural area, tractor driver, a known carrier of the HIV virus since 2010, however without previous follow-up, contacted us for the first time at Fundacao de Medicina Tropical Dr. Heitor Vieira Dourado, Manaus, Amazonas, Brazil, for investigation of left knee chronic monoarthritis associated with tegumentary lesions. He had been using zidovudine, lamivudine, lopinavir/ritonavir for three weeks, this being the first antiretroviral regimen used. He had never used prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. He denied being a smoker or alcohol user. He reported that the left knee arthritis appeared after local trauma identified five months before, preceding the tegumentary lesions that appeared two months after the fact. During the clinic exam, polymorphism of skin lesions was noted with pustules of follicular distribution, papules with central necrosis, erythematous-infiltrated plaques covered with pustules and ulcerated plaques, located on the face, trunk, abdomen and limbs, associated with left knee arthritis (Figures 1, 2 and 3A). Oral and genital mucosa were spared. Lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly were not observed. Blood cultures for aerobes, mycobacteria, fungi and leukocyte cream were negative. VDRL resulted non-reagent. The Leishmaniasis screening exam was negative. The analysis of synovial fluid suggested infectious arthritis. Left knee x-ray showed reduction of joint space and osteolytic patellar lesion (Figure 3B). Patient underwent surgical cleansing of joint, biopsy of synovial membrane and skin. Both exams identified round cells, birefringent, with multiple buddings compatible with P. brasiliensis (Figure 4). Culture of synovial tissue confirmed the finding. Complementary propedeutics suggested pulmonary involvement and the Xpert/MTB RIF  sputum test was negative. At the time of diagnosis T CD4+ count was 44 cells/mm3 . Patient was treated with Amphotericin B deoxycholate 50mg/day (cumulative dose of 650mg) but despite the therapy, his clinical condition worsened, progressing to death on the 20th day of hospitalization. Necropsy revealed involvement of lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, adrenals and bone marrow, in addition to the previously described sites (Figure 5).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old male presenting with chronic left knee monoarthritis for 5 months and polymorphic cutaneous lesions for 3 months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed progressive pain and swelling in the left knee following local trauma 5 months prior. Two months later, he noticed the appearance of polymorphic skin lesions that progressively spread across his face, trunk, abdomen, and extremities. Three weeks prior to consultation, he initiated his first combination antiretroviral regimen.
subjective.past_medical_history: Chronic retroviral illness diagnosed in 2010 without prior clinical follow-up or opportunistic prophylaxis; initiated on zidovudine, lamivudine, and lopinavir/ritonavir 3 weeks prior. Denied tobacco or alcohol consumption. Occupation: tractor driver; epidemiological exposure: leisure activities in a rural area of Santarém, Pará, Brazilian Amazon.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for left knee pain, swelling, and diffuse skin lesions; negative for oral or genital ulcers, fever, or weight loss. Home medications: zidovudine, lamivudine, lopinavir/ritonavir. Allergies: unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatologic: extensive polymorphic cutaneous eruption consisting of pustules in a follicular distribution, papules with central necrosis, erythematous-infiltrated plaques covered with pustules, and ulcerated plaques over face, trunk, abdomen, and limbs; oral and genital mucosa completely spared. Musculoskeletal: inflammatory monoarthritis of the left knee with effusion, warmth, and restricted range of motion. Lymph nodes and abdomen: no lymphadenopathy; no hepatosplenomegaly.
objective.routine_investigations: Blood cultures for aerobes, mycobacteria, fungi, and leukocyte buffy coat: negative. Syphilis VDRL: non-reactive. Leishmaniasis screening test: negative. Sputum Xpert MTB/RIF: negative for tuberculosis. Synovial fluid analysis: cloudy fluid consistent with infectious arthritis. Left knee plain radiograph: joint space narrowing with an osteolytic patellar lesion.
objective.advanced_workup: Arthroscopic surgical debridement and synovial membrane biopsy; skin punch biopsy. Histopathology of skin and synovium: round, birefringent yeast cells with multiple peripheral buddings ('pilot wheel' / 'mariner's wheel' appearance) characteristic of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis. Synovial tissue culture: confirmed Paracoccidioides brasiliensis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Disseminated paracoccidioidomycosis presenting with chronic osteoarticular infection (patellar osteolytic monoarthritis), severe polymorphic cutaneomucosal lesions, and pulmonary involvement in advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) / AIDS (CD4+ T-cell count 44 cells/mm3). Visceral leishmaniasis, syphilis, tuberculosis, and pyogenic/bacterial septic arthritis excluded by negative serology, cultures, and sputum Xpert MTB/RIF. Paracoccidioidomycosis confirmed by biopsy of synovial membrane and skin showing birefringent multiple-budding yeast cells and positive synovial fungal cultures. Management & Outcome: Underwent surgical joint cleansing and received intravenous amphotericin B deoxycholate 50 mg/day (cumulative dose 650 mg). Despite antifungal therapy, clinical condition deteriorated with multisystem failure, leading to death on hospital day 20. Post-mortem necropsy confirmed disseminated paracoccidioidomycosis involving lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, adrenal glands, bone marrow, synovium, and skin.
